correctness.rationale: The polar nondegeneracy gives a two-valued quadratic Gauss sum and the exact character-shift identity. Direct multiplication of two level-set indicators yields all Weyl ambiguity coefficients K, L, h or 0, including the endpoint m=1. Symmetric Walsh–Weyl matrices are exactly those with b(a)=0, giving a full orthogonal basis and a diagonal lift whose multiplicities add to N(N+1)/2. A direct spectral collision test yields only m=2,rho=-1 as a projective 2-design. The exact standard-library checker verifies 17,472 finite amplitudes and both 16-dimensional second-moment operators, supporting but not replacing the algebraic proof. The domain is explicitly real symmetric.

originality.rationale: The primary historical Gabor phase-retrieval theorem treats cyclic full complex-operator measurements under a nonzero-ambiguity criterion, and classical bent difference-set constructions do not state full real symmetric lifting rank/spectrum. The closest published hyperbolic quadratic Gabor result assumes odd characteristic; the closest binary quadric spectral result treats first-band linear Fourier restriction. Their full texts were inspected and compared by mathematical implication. Multiple actual semantic searches for binary quadratic level-set projector orbits, equivalences and 16-dimensional projective designs did not reveal a covering theorem. This is a best-knowledge conclusion with stated nonzero historical-priority risk, not an automatic novelty guarantee.
residual_risks: A more general, historically stated group-covariant real design or Weyl-tomography theorem may imply this result after translating its hypotheses; no exhaustive global theorem census is claimed.
The small (16,6,2) difference-set parameters and quadratic bentness are known; originality is claimed only for the full real Gabor lifting spectrum, conditioning and unique design resonance.
The real full-symmetric-space conclusion does not extend verbatim to complex phase retrieval.

value.rationale: Finite difference sets and bent quadratic supports are natural sources of short-time Fourier windows. The exact all-dimension rank and sharp lift condition number resolve whether these highly structured non-generic, real-valued windows permit stable real symmetric tomography; they distinguish a true signal-recovery problem from simpler support/difference-set counting. The precisely isolated m=2, rho=-1 spectral collision produces an explicit 256-vector real projective 2-design and fourth-moment identity. Neither structural result is a routine renamed parameter or an unmotivated small-dimensional enumeration.
